newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: GLOBE SAYS RAISING 97 CAPEX TO 8 BLN PESOS.
newsitem.headline: GLOBE SAYS RAISING 97 CAPEX TO 8 BLN PESOS.

text.p: Globe Telecom GMCR Inc said on Tuesday it was raising its 1997 capital expenditure to eight billion pesos from an original 4.7 billion.
Globe chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala told reporters the company was going to be very aggressive in installing new land lines and cell sites for its mobile phone network.
"We've opted to adopt a very aggressive rollout plan." Ayala said after a special stockholders meting of Ayala Corp.
Globe is a joint venture of Ayala Corp and Singapore Telecom.
Other Globe officials said the increased capital expenditure was necessary to fight growing competition.
"From the marketing point of view, we need to have a stable network to compete," said chief financial officer Gil Genio.
The higher capital expenditure for this year would mean an acceleration of Globe's expansion plans.
Genio said Globe had originally planned to spend 20 billion pesos over four years, starting 1997.
The firm intends to have 300 cell sites by the early part of next year from 106 at the end of 1996.
At the end of July, Globe had 63,000 fixed lines.
Genio said half of the 20 billion-peso capital expenditure would be funded by stock rights and warrants.
Bank of America offered to raise the rest of the funding requirements, he said.
